prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Phoenix after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Phoenix for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific firms — and stronger recommendations — but first a couple quick questions so I tailor the list:

- What part of Phoenix or what ZIP code are you in?  
- Were you injured (ambulance/ER visit) or is it mostly vehicle/property damage?  
- Do you prefer a large national firm or a smaller local boutique firm?

While you answer, here are immediate, practical next steps and a few reliable ways to find good Phoenix personal injury lawyers right now:

1) One national firm with an established Phoenix presence to consider
- Morgan & Morgan — large national personal injury firm that advertises Phoenix services and handles car accidents on contingency. Good if you want a firm with lots of resources and experience handling large caseloads.

2) Use local referral and review resources (to find highly rated local firms)
- Arizona State Bar Lawyer Referral Service — they can refer you to screened attorneys in your area.
- Super Lawyers (Arizona) and Avvo — offer attorney profiles, peer ratings, client reviews and practice-area filters.
- Google/Yelp — look at recent client reviews and how the firm responds.

3) What to ask on the first call (so you can compare firms quickly)
- Do you handle car-accident/personal-injury cases exclusively? (Prefer attorneys who mainly handle PI.)
- What is your contingency fee and are there other costs I would be responsible for if we don’t recover?  
- How long have you handled cases like mine and have you taken any to trial?  
- Typical range of settlements/verdicts for cases like mine (they can’t promise, but experienced lawyers will discuss similar outcomes).  
- Who will be my direct point of contact and how often will I get updates?  
- Do you handle lien negotiation with medical providers/insurers?

4) Immediate do’s and don’ts after a crash
- Do get medical care and keep all records/receipts.  
- Do preserve photos of the scene, damage, injuries, and contact info for witnesses.  
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other party’s insurer or sign releases without a lawyer.  
- Don’t delay contacting a lawyer — statute of limitations in Arizona for personal injury is usually 2 years from the date of injury.

If you tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and whether you prefer big-firm or boutique, I’ll provide 5-7 specific Phoenix-area personal-injury firms (names, phone numbers to call, and a short reason to call each).
